stem: A SQL pipeline validates transaction rows where a numeric column sometimes carries a stray currency symbol, as in the literal '100$'. The team must keep the query running and land a null for those rows rather than have the statement fail.

option_texts.A: CAST returns a null for the malformed literal and the query keeps running
option_texts.B: TRY_CAST returns a null for the malformed literal instead of raising an invalid data error
option_texts.C: CAST silently truncates the malformed literal to 100 and the query keeps running
option_texts.D: Both functions raise an error, so the rows must be filtered in a WHERE clause first

drill_answer_short: try_cast returns NULL for input that is invalid for the target type, where cast raises the error
decision_hinge: try_cast returns NULL instead of an invalid data error, while cast returns an error when the input is invalid for the target type.

plausible_options.A: keep the query running and land a null for those rows

eliminated_by.C: a numeric column sometimes carries a stray currency symbol
eliminated_by.D: rather than have the statement fail

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - cast is the function that raises on invalid input, try_cast is the one that returns null
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - cast does not truncate a malformed literal to its leading digits
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - try_cast exists precisely so the statement does not have to fail

stem: A data engineer wants a relational object that joins two tables for ad hoc work in the current notebook session only. Nothing should persist once the session ends, and no other user should be able to see the object.

option_texts.A: CREATE VIEW, because a standard view exists only for the connection that defined it
option_texts.B: CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW, because such views are visible only to the session that created them
option_texts.C: CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY VIEW, so the object lives in a cluster-wide temporary schema
option_texts.D: CREATE TABLE, then DROP TABLE at the end of the notebook session

drill_answer_short: A TEMPORARY view is visible only to the creating session and is dropped when that session ends
decision_hinge: TEMPORARY views are visible only to the session that created them and are dropped when the session ends.

plausible_options.C: Nothing should persist once the session ends

eliminated_by.A: joins two tables for ad hoc work in the current notebook session only
eliminated_by.D: no other user should be able to see the object

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - a standard view is a persistent catalog object, not a connection-scoped one
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - a global temporary view is deliberately shared, which breaks the privacy requirement
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - a real table persists in the metastore for as long as it exists

stem: An existing Delta table named transactions was created without any column constraints. The team must now guarantee that transaction_id and transaction_date never hold a null, without recreating the table.

option_texts.A: Run ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN to add the NOT NULL constraint after creation
option_texts.B: Run ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT with a CHECK expression testing each column for a null
option_texts.C: Recreate the table with the constraint declared in the schema and reload the rows
option_texts.D: Set a table property that rejects nulls on write for the two named columns

drill_answer_short: NOT NULL is declared in the schema at creation; to add it afterwards use ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN
decision_hinge: When you create a table you specify NOT NULL constraints in the schema, and to drop or add NOT NULL constraints after creation you use the ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN command.

plausible_options.B: guarantee that transaction_id and transaction_date never hold a null

eliminated_by.D: was created without any column constraints

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a CHECK constraint can test for a null, but NOT NULL is the declared constraint the team asked for
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the table must not be recreated
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no table property turns null rejection on for named columns

stem: A silver table declares a primary key on customer_id. A later load inserts two rows carrying the same customer_id and the write succeeds. The team must explain why the declaration did not block the duplicate.

option_texts.A: A primary key on Databricks is informational only and is not enforced on write
option_texts.B: A primary key is enforced only when the table also carries a CHECK constraint
option_texts.C: A primary key is enforced, but the duplicate landed because the write bypassed the constraint
option_texts.D: A primary key is enforced only on a managed table, and this one is external

drill_answer_short: Primary key, foreign key and unique constraints are informational only and are not enforced
decision_hinge: Primary key, foreign key, and unique constraints are informational only and aren't enforced, while enforced constraints verify data integrity before adding rows to a table.

plausible_options.C: inserts two rows carrying the same customer_id and the write succeeds

eliminated_by.B: The team must explain why the declaration did not block the duplicate
eliminated_by.D: A silver table declares a primary key on customer_id

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - a CHECK constraint does not switch on primary key enforcement
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - there is no enforcement to bypass, the constraint is informational
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - managed and external tables differ in storage, not in constraint enforcement

stem: A silver table must reject any row whose order_amount is negative, and the rule has to live on the table itself so every writer is bound by it. The team does not want the rule expressed only inside one pipeline's query.

option_texts.A: Add a CHECK constraint, whose boolean expression must be true for each input row
option_texts.B: Add a NOT NULL constraint on order_amount so the column refuses the bad values
option_texts.C: Add a pipeline expectation that drops the offending rows as they flow through
option_texts.D: Add a primary key on order_amount so a negative value cannot be written twice

drill_answer_short: A CHECK constraint holds a boolean expression that must be true for every input row, and it lives on the table
decision_hinge: A CHECK constraint indicates that a specified boolean expression must be true for each input row, and when a constraint is violated the transaction fails with an error.

plausible_options.C: must reject any row whose order_amount is negative

eliminated_by.B: the rule has to live on the table itself so every writer is bound by it
eliminated_by.D: The team does not want the rule expressed only inside one pipeline's query

distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - NOT NULL rejects a missing value, not a negative one
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - an expectation does enforce quality, but only inside the pipeline that declares it
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a primary key is informational and says nothing about sign

stem: A Delta table has accumulated many data files that no version of the table references any more, and cloud storage cost has grown. The team must delete those files while keeping the table queryable at its current version.

option_texts.A: Run OPTIMIZE, which compacts small files and deletes the ones left behind
option_texts.B: Run VACUUM, which removes data files no longer referenced and older than the retention threshold
option_texts.C: Run DELETE on the table, which clears the files the table stopped referencing
option_texts.D: Run CLEAN, which purges stale data files from the table directory

drill_answer_short: vacuum removes data files no longer referenced by a table that are older than the retention threshold
decision_hinge: Running vacuum removes data files no longer referenced by a table that are older than the retention threshold, and deleting unused data files reduces cloud storage costs.

plausible_options.A: must delete those files while keeping the table queryable at its current version

eliminated_by.C: no version of the table references any more

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - OPTIMIZE compacts the layout but leaves the superseded files on storage
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - DELETE removes rows and adds new versions, it does not purge files
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - there is no CLEAN command for a Delta table

stem: An engineer runs vacuum on a Delta table with the default retention threshold, then tries to read a version of the table from two months ago for an audit. The read fails, and the team must understand what the maintenance command changed.

option_texts.A: The vacuum run rewrote the table history, so the audit versions left DESCRIBE HISTORY
option_texts.B: The ability to query table versions older than the retention period is lost after vacuum
option_texts.C: The table became a managed table, so the retention settings moved with its storage
option_texts.D: The audit version is intact and simply needs a timestamp rather than a version number

drill_answer_short: Once vacuum runs, versions older than the retention period can no longer be queried
decision_hinge: The ability to query table versions older than the retention period is lost after running vacuum.

plausible_options.D: tries to read a version of the table from two months ago for an audit

eliminated_by.A: the team must understand what the maintenance command changed
eliminated_by.C: runs vacuum on a Delta table with the default retention threshold

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - the vacuum run removes data files rather than rewriting history entries
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - vacuum does not convert a table to managed storage
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - either addressing form fails once the underlying files are gone

stem: A team keeps a large external table in Unity Catalog and now wants Databricks to manage its storage and lifecycle. The conversion must happen in place on the existing table rather than through a rebuild.

option_texts.A: Use ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED, choosing MOVE or COPY for the underlying files
option_texts.B: Use ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED to hand storage control over to Databricks
option_texts.C: Use CREATE TABLE AS SELECT into a managed table and then drop the external one
option_texts.D: Use ALTER TABLE ... SET LOCATION to point the table at a managed storage path

drill_answer_short: ALTER TABLE SET MANAGED, with MOVE or COPY, converts an existing external table in place
decision_hinge: The ALTER TABLE SET MANAGED clause, with MOVE or COPY, converts an existing table to a managed table, and UNSET MANAGED is the clause that reverses it.

plausible_options.C: wants Databricks to manage its storage and lifecycle

eliminated_by.B: keeps a large external table in Unity Catalog
eliminated_by.D: must happen in place on the existing table rather than through a rebuild

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - UNSET MANAGED runs the conversion in the opposite direction
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - a rebuild produces a managed table but replaces the object instead of converting it
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - SET LOCATION repoints an external table and does not change who manages it

stem: A gold view's defining query must change, and a dozen analyst groups already hold SELECT on it. The team must apply the new query without having to re-grant anything afterwards.

option_texts.A: Run DROP VIEW then CREATE VIEW, and re-apply the grants from a saved script
option_texts.B: Run CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, which changes the view in place without dropping its privileges
option_texts.C: Run ALTER VIEW with the new query text, without disturbing the grants on the view
option_texts.D: Run CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS, which updates the definition when the view exists

drill_answer_short: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW changes a view in place and keeps its privileges
decision_hinge: Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW to change a view in place without dropping its privileges.

plausible_options.C: must apply the new query without having to re-grant anything afterwards

eliminated_by.A: a dozen analyst groups already hold SELECT on it
eliminated_by.D: A gold view's defining query must change

distractor_traps.A: T2: scope error - dropping the view discards the grants, which is the outcome being avoided
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - ALTER VIEW changes metadata such as the name, not the defining query
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - IF NOT EXISTS skips the statement when the view is already there

stem: A production multi-task job must alert the on-call rota the moment a run fails. The team already runs its paging through PagerDuty and wants the alert to reach that tool rather than a mailbox.

option_texts.A: Configure a notification on the Failure event and send it to a system destination
option_texts.B: Configure a notification on the Failure event, since email is the only supported channel
option_texts.C: Configure a webhook task at the end of the job that fires only when a task has failed
option_texts.D: Configure an alert in Databricks SQL, which is where job run failures are published

drill_answer_short: Job notifications can go to email or to a third-party system destination such as PagerDuty
decision_hinge: You can send notifications to one or more email addresses or third-party destinations such as Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, or any webhook-based service, and an administrator must configure system destinations.

plausible_options.C: wants the alert to reach that tool rather than a mailbox

eliminated_by.B: The team already runs its paging through PagerDuty
eliminated_by.D: must alert the on-call rota the moment a run fails

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - third-party destinations are supported alongside email
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - a trailing task can post a message, but it is not the built-in notification path
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - Databricks SQL alerts watch query results, not job run outcomes
